questions.question: Transitioning a property requires the property to be:
questions.explanation: Only animatable properties interpolate. display, position, and visibility aren't (use opacity/transform instead).

questions.question: transition-property: transform, opacity means:

options.text: Only those two properties will animate on change

questions.explanation: List the specific properties to transition; others change instantly. 'all' targets everything (can cause unintended transitions).

questions.question: If you change a property WITHOUT a transition declared, it:
questions.explanation: Transitions only interpolate when a transition is set for that property and a duration > 0; otherwise the change is immediate.

questions.question: A transition defined ONLY on :hover will:

options.text: Animate IN on hover, but snap back instantly when unhovered

questions.explanation: The transition must exist on the base state to also animate the return; otherwise only the hover-in tween occurs.

questions.question: transition-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) is a:

options.text: Custom easing curve defined by 4 control values

questions.explanation: cubic-bezier lets you craft precise easing (this one is the common 'standard' material curve).

questions.question: Multiple transitions with different durations use:
questions.explanation: transition: color .3s, transform .6s applies per-property timing via comma lists aligned to transition-property.

questions.question: Transitions are commonly triggered by:

options.text: State changes like :hover, :focus, class toggles, or attribute changes

questions.explanation: Any change to a transitioned property value triggers the tween — typically via pseudo-classes or JS-toggled classes.

questions.question: For a reveal effect you should animate:

options.text: opacity and transform (not display/visibility) for smoothness

questions.explanation: display can't tween; fade with opacity and slide with transform, toggling visibility/opacity for accessibility.
